# Proposal 2 · §6–10 Navigation → library

DESIGN PROPOSAL · PART 2 OF 5 · §6–10

## 6 Navigation

| Need | Primary | Also |
|---|---|---|
| Previous / next page | Keys, wheel, trackpad, tap zones, swipes (§5) | Desktop margins are click targets; a faint chevron shows on hover |
| Previous / next chapter | ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ (Alt on Windows / Linux); single-key [ ] where the layout has them | Contents tab; scrubber |
| Table of contents | ⌘T or the list button | “Go to chapter…” in ⌘K |
| Reading progress | Optional one-line location at rest; scrubber with the chrome | “Time left in chapter” from the reader’s own pace |
| Jump to a percentage | Drag the scrubber; a tooltip previews chapter and % Screen 03 | Click the location label or ⌘J → Go to: %, chapter or print page Screen 17 |
| Return to previous location | Back: ⌘[ · Alt+← · mouse back button | A “Back to page 43” chip after every jump (10 s, pauses on hover or focus) |
| Internal links | Jump and push history | Back chip |
| Footnotes | A noteref opens a peek anchored to the marker; it never navigates Screen 17 | “Open note” in the peek for long notes |
| External links | System browser; URL shown on hover or long-press | No in-app browser |

### When controls appear

| Reveal method | Decision |
|---|---|
| Always visible | **No.** An attention cost on every page. |
| Any pointer movement | **No.** Hands rest on the mouse; small nudges would flash the chrome. |
| Pointer at top or bottom edge (150 ms dwell) | **Yes, desktop.** Reveals that bar only. In macOS full screen the top zone starts below the system menu bar; the bottom zone is off when the Dock or taskbar auto-hides at that edge. |
| Centre tap | **Yes, touch.** Toggles both bars. |
| Keyboard | **Yes.** Tab reveals the chrome and focuses its first control; Esc hides it and returns focus to the text. Space turns a page only when the text has focus — on a focused button it presses the button. |
| Auto-hide | On page turn, or 3 s after the pointer leaves an edge; never while a control has focus or a popover is open. |

Reveal is intentional, local and reversible. The two bars hold eight controls between them; the reading screen never becomes a toolbar.

## 7 Search

**Recommendation: a tab in the Navigator sidebar** Screen 05. An overlay would hide the page the results refer to; a popover is too small for grouped results; a dedicated screen breaks context. A sidebar keeps results and text visible together, and shares its slot with Contents and Notes: one place for “go somewhere in this book”.

| Aspect | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Entry | ⌘F, the search button, or “Search in book” in ⌘K. A current selection pre-fills the field. |
| Incremental | Runs 150 ms after typing stops, from 2 characters (1 for CJK). Ignores case and diacritics; quotes match exact phrases. |
| Order | Current chapter first, then onward, wrapping — the nearest hits arrive first. |
| Indexing | Built in a background worker on first search, then cached. While it runs the header reads “Searching 38 of 135 chapters”; typing is never blocked. |
| Count and snippets | “14 results in 5 chapters”, updating live. Snippets of about 90 characters, cut at word boundaries, match emphasised. |
| Grouping | By chapter with counts; the current chapter expanded and marked, the rest collapsible. |
| In the text | Every visible match gets a soft tint and a 1 px outline (3.8:1), the active one a stronger tint and a 2 px accent outline. Search marks are outlined, highlights underlined, so the two never look alike. |
| Next / previous | ↵ / ⇧↵ in the field; ⌘G / ⇧⌘G anywhere; ↑ ↓ move through results and the page follows. |
| Closing | Esc. If you only browsed, you return to your original page; if you chose a result, you stay, and Back returns you. Marks clear on close. |

Deferred: regular expressions, whole-word matching, search across the library.

## 8 Text selection, highlighting and annotation

Select → selection bar → colour (saved) → optional margin note (autosaves) → revisit from the Notes tab or by clicking the highlight

**Selection bar** Screen 06. Four colour dots, Note, Copy, Search, and “⋯” for extension actions such as Define. It sits 12 px above the first selected line and flips below when there is less than 56 px above; it never covers the selection. It is ink-coloured so it reads clearly as interface, not text (inverted to a light surface at Night Screen 14). Core actions render immediately; extension actions are appended when ready. The bar is announced as “Selection actions, F6”; F6 moves focus into it, arrow keys move between actions, and Esc returns focus to the selection.

**Highlights.** Clicking a colour saves — no confirmation. The four colours carry no fixed meaning (naming them comes later). Every highlight is a tint plus a 2 px underline in a darker shade (3.5–4.9:1 against Paper and Sepia), so it stays visible to low-vision readers and never relies on hue alone; at Night the tint is fainter because solid blocks glare on dark ground. Lists always name the colour. H or ⇧⌘H applies the last-used colour. A plain click on a highlight opens its actions; a drag that starts on one begins a new selection.

**Notes** Screen 07. A note always belongs to a highlight. When the margin is wide enough (windows of 1240 px and up) the note card opens beside the passage, not over it; below that, and on tablets, it is a bottom sheet that leaves the passage visible Screen 15. It saves as you type; Esc or a click elsewhere closes it; an empty note is discarded and the highlight kept. A small margin dot marks passages with notes.

**Editing and deleting.** Clicking a highlight reopens the bar with colour, note, copy and delete. Delete is immediate, with an Undo message and ⌘Z — never a confirmation dialog. The message lasts 10 s, pauses while pointed at or focused, is announced to screen readers, and stays reachable afterwards under ⌘K › Recently closed Screen 16.

**Annotation list** Screen 08. The Notes tab lists highlights by chapter in reading order, filterable by colour and text. Choosing one jumps to the passage, pulses it for 1.2 s and offers Back. Highlights that can’t be re-anchored, for example after the book file changes, are listed under “Couldn’t place” with their quote — never dropped silently.

**Storage and export.** Annotations are stored as W3C Web Annotation–compatible JSON with two selectors, an EPUB CFI and a text quote with prefix and suffix, so they survive reflow and book updates. The MVP ships one exporter, Markdown, built as an extension to prove the pipeline; JSON, Readwise and Obsidian exports can follow as extensions.

| Input | Select | Act |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse | Drag; double-click a word; triple-click a paragraph | Bar on mouse-up; right-click gives the native context menu with the same actions |
| Trackpad | As mouse; force-click keeps macOS Look Up | Bar on release |
| Touch | Long-press, then system handles | On iPad our actions join the system edit menu instead of competing with it; elsewhere the bar sits below the selection, clear of fingers and handles |
| Keyboard | Caret browsing (F7) with ⇧ + arrows; screen-reader users select with their reader’s own commands | F6 into the bar; H / ⇧⌘H highlight, N / ⇧⌘N note, Esc cancel |

## 9 Typography and reading settings

The Aa popover Screen 09 has four rows and nothing else: **size** (a stepped slider, also ⌘− ⌘+ ⌘0), **theme** (Paper, Sepia, Night, Auto), **line spacing** (Compact, Normal, Loose) and **layout** (Pages or Scroll). Size, theme and spacing are global because they reflect eyesight and surroundings, not the book; layout is remembered per book. Every row states its scope (“All books” or “This book”). One link at the bottom leads to Preferences.

| Setting | Release | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Size, theme, line spacing, Pages / Scroll | **MVP** | Cover most comfort needs |
| Font family: book default, Literata, a sans, a dyslexia-friendly face | 1.1 | Needs licensing and a reliable override of publisher fonts |
| Page width: narrow, normal, wide | 1.1 | Matters on very large monitors; the default clamp comes first |
| Publisher styles: full, balanced, off | 1.1 | The escape hatch for badly styled books |
| Paragraph spacing, justification, hyphenation, weight, margins | Later | Each multiplies the test matrix against publisher CSS |
| Custom themes | Via extensions | Declarative token packs, no code |

Every new control has to beat the default for a real group of readers; otherwise it belongs in an extension.

## 10 Library design

**The smallest useful model is one screen** Screen 01: a Continue reading row with the current book large and the next two small, then an All books cover grid. The header holds search (title and author), sort (Recent, Title, Author) and Open… — nothing else.

| Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Grid or list | Grid in MVP; list view in 1.1 | Covers are the fastest recognition cue in small and medium libraries |
| Tile | Cover, title (2 lines), author, progress bar with %, or “New” / “Finished” | Enough to choose; last-opened time appears only under Continue reading |
| Missing cover | Generated typographic cover, tint derived from the title | No grey placeholder boxes |
| Organisation | Search and sort only | Collections, tags and series wait for evidence of need |
| Item menu | Book info, Show in Finder / Explorer, Remove | Rare actions stay out of sight |

**Into reading with minimal friction.** One click or tap opens a book; the cover grows into the page in 240 ms and the book opens at its saved position. “Resume reading” is the default button, so Return opens the current book straight from launch. Opening an .epub from the OS skips the library entirely.
